requirements.quote:
There are cryptographic limits on the amount of plaintext which can
   be safely encrypted under a given set of keys.  [AEAD-LIMITS]
   provides an analysis of these limits under the assumption that the
   underlying primitive (AES or ChaCha20) has no weaknesses.
   Implementations SHOULD do a key update as described in Section 4.6.3
   prior to reaching these limits.
requirements.condition: the active traffic keys are approaching their cryptographic usage limit
requirements.required_behavior: perform a KeyUpdate before reaching the limit
requirements.why_checkable: Per-key record accounting and the update threshold can be inspected and tested.

requirements.quote:
For AES-GCM, up to 2^24.5 full-size records (about 24 million) may be
   encrypted on a given connection while keeping a safety margin of
   approximately 2^-57 for Authenticated Encryption (AE) security.  For
requirements.condition: AES-GCM protects full-size records under one key set on a connection
requirements.required_behavior: treat 2^24.5 records as the stated per-key safety limit
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue using the same keys beyond the stated safety limit without update or closure
requirements.why_checkable: A counter can enforce the numeric AES-GCM usage threshold referenced by the update requirement.
